title: Query statistics: finding what costs the most in total, not per run

videos.script: Somebody tells you the database is slow. Which query? {{which}} Most people answer by guessing. They pick the query that looked slow the last time they ran it by hand, or the one behind the screen that got the complaint. {{guess}} The server does not guess. Every statement it runs, it can count: how many times, for how long in total, how many rows. {{counts}} This lesson switches that counting on, and then gives the server a morning's work. Six kinds of request, the way an application sends them, a thousand a second, for one minute. {{workload}} Then you read the score. And the first thing it teaches is that the slowest query is usually not the one costing the most. {{score}} A query that takes two hundred milliseconds and runs a few times an hour hardly matters. One that takes thirty and runs a hundred times a second is where the server's day goes. {{total}} By the end you will have found a missing index from the outside, fixed it, and measured that the fix did what you thought. {{fix}} That is the loop this whole course repeats. Count first. Then change one thing. Then count again. {{title}}
